summary: This work introduces quantum LDPC codes with design rate $1/5$ constructed from balanced products of classical codes with non-abelian $\mathbb{Z}_{\ell_1} \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_{\ell_2}$ (ZSZ) group symmetries, achieving code-capacity memory efficiency $kd^2/n$ superior to prior constructions for block lengths below 1000 physical qubits. Under idling-free circuit-level depolarizing noise at $0.1\%$ strength with GPU-accelerated Relay-belief-propagation decoding, ZSZ-LP codes with $d \in \{10,12,14,16,18\}$ approach the gigaquop and teraquop regimes with latencies of 1–2 ms, and syndrome extraction on reconfigurable atom arrays requires 30–60 ms rearrangement overhead per round.
motivation: Constant-rate quantum LDPC codes promise constant spatial overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but discovering finite-length instances with practical performance remains challenging. Prior work showed that abelian group algebras suffer from distance bounds of $O(1)$ in the 5-block construction; this work exploits non-abelian groups to circumvent that obstruction.
method: ZSZ-LP codes are constructed via balanced product of pairs of classical $(3,6)$-regular LDPC codes (ZSZ-2BGA codes with rate $1/2$ and minimum distances 10–22) that share free ZSZ group actions. Classical codes are found by filtered random search over trinomial pairs with girth and distance criteria. Logical Pauli bases are constructed as group orbits, yielding one-generator-minimal (OGM) and one-generator-symplectic (OGS) forms. Syndrome extraction schedules are optimized for optical tweezers via a greedy AOD routing algorithm.
result: ZSZ-LP-320 ($\langle 320, 64, 14 \rangle$) and ZSZ-LP-390 ($\langle 390, 78, \leq 16 \rangle$) achieve per-qubit-round logical error rates of $2.3 \times 10^{-11}$ and $2 \times 10^{-12}$ respectively at $p=0.1\%$; ZSZ-LP-550 extrapolates to $10^{-13}$ regimes. Classical ZSZ-2BGA codes show $95\%$-ile minimum distances exceeding those of configuration-model and PEG ensembles at lengths up to 310, with pseudothreshold near 1.25 dB on AWGN-BPSK, within 1.1 dB of Shannon limit for rate $1/2$.
